materiality_analysis.reason: The disclosure reverses the primary driver of lending and deposit-related fees. In 2023, fees increased primarily due to amortization of First Republic discounts. In 2024, this amortization declined significantly as commitments expired, and the growth in fees is now attributed to organic drivers like higher deposit volume and cash management fees in Payments. This signals a transition from acquisition-driven accounting effects to organic volume growth.
